Tune quality knobs#

Every quality decision in the viewer has a URL knob. Append them to any playground or share link (https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk&ssr=1&hdr=0) to A/B a look, pin a result for a client, or bisect a performance problem. Nothing here is required — the defaults are tuned per device tier (tier A: WebGPU on a desktop-class GPU; tier B: WebGPU on a phone or tablet; tier C: the WebGL2 build — Concepts) — but a link with a knob always renders the same way, which is what you want when you send one.

The table#

KnobValuesDefaultUse it when
?ssr=0…1, or bare ?ssrauto: 0.5 on bake-dominant archviz scenes, 0 elsewhere (tier A only)Glossy floors and tables should mirror the room. Half-resolution screen-space reflections; 0 kills the pass, 1 is strongest. Off on tier B regardless.
?sheen=0…1, or bare ?sheen (= 0.15)offA fully-baked (unlit) scene reads flat and dead on glossy furniture. Adds a low-intensity IBL specular over lightmapped materials without touching the bake's colours.
?hdr=auto · 1 · 0 (+ ?hdrpeak= 1–8, default 2)auto in the playground, SDR in embedsOn an HDR display, hot speculars and emissives past 1.0 should use real headroom (auto enables when the panel reports dynamic-range: high and the device is tier A). 0 pins SDR — set it for anything destined for SDR screens, including video exports. 1 forces the float16 surface anywhere.
?exposure=EV stops (clamped ±4) or auto0The scene is too dark or too hot as authored. auto is a one-shot scene-adaptive nudge toward mid-grey; a number is a fixed offset you can put in a link.
?env=studio · sky, optionally ,<intensity>studioLit (non-baked) scenes: studio is a three-softbox rig that flatters products; sky is the outdoor preset. env=sky,1.5 brightens the environment 1.5×. Ignored by bake-dominant scenes (their lighting is the bake).
?post=full · leantier A full, tier B leanTier B defaults to a lean post chain (depth of field and bloom skipped, TSR kept) for frame time. post=full opts a tier-B device back in; post=lean forces lean on tier A to measure the cost.
?render=demand · continuouscontinuous (playground), demand (embeds and devices on battery)demand renders only while something changes — input, tours, animations, streaming refinement — and parks the loop otherwise, so a still viewer costs ~zero battery. The HUD fps reads "idle" when parked. continuous is the classic every-vsync loop.
?profile=1flagoffYou need to know where frame time goes. Per-pass GPU timings in an overlay and window.__versePassMs (cull, vg-cull, shadow, sky+ext, main-a (mesh opaques), vg-depth (streamed depth prepass + alpha cut), vg-opaque, hiz+cull2, main-b, oit, ssao, ssr, tsr, bloom, blit, frame); the frame row is the honest total on tile-based GPUs, where passes overlap. While profiling, main pass A is split at those draw groups (a few tile loads/stores more). Tier C reports shadow, sky+ext, main-a, vg-opaque, transparent, post through EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 where the browser exposes it.
?upscale=0 · 1on for a .vpk ≥ 512 MB on WebGPU (tier A, B)Temporal upscaling for big scenes: TSR (jittered, history-reprojected, neighbourhood-clamped, sharpened) replaces 4× MSAA, the scene renders at ≤ 0.75 of native while the camera moves and climbs back to native when it is still. 0 keeps MSAA; 1 turns it on for any scene.
?scale=0.5…1dynamic (DRS)A/B tests and screenshots. Pins the internal render scale and disables dynamic resolution; scale=1 vs scale=0.6 separates pixel-bound passes from resolution-independent ones. Video export pins it to 1 for you.
?tbn=1flagoffClassic (non-streamed) PBR models with normal maps over irregular or sheared UV unwraps. Shades from the authored or mikktspace vertex tangent frame instead of the screen-space cotangent frame. Measured a wash on the reference helmet, which is why it is opt-in.
?vgflat=0flagonYou want to see the streamed scene's early frames exactly as the final texture would render them. Default on shades the first, coarse clusters with their baked flat colour so the first seconds read as a soft clay model with correct colours instead of shattered texture glass; 0 disables that early-shading pass.

Related knobs in the same family: ?ssao=0 / ?ao=<strength>[,<radius>] (ambient occlusion), ?dof=<focus m>,<aperture> (depth of field), ?sun=<azimuth>,<elevation>[,<intensity>] (time of day, moves shading and shadows together), ?material=<idx>:<rrggbb>;… (finish variants), ?oit=0 (in-pass alpha instead of order-independent transparency), ?tier=c (force the WebGL2 fallback), ?quality=4k / ?temporal=1 (temporal super-resolution).

Quality switches: ?gi=0 (real-time GI off), ?vt=0 (the pre-virtual-texturing texture path), ?refl=0 (per-room reflection probes off — the environment reflections instead), ?rt=1 (ray-traced reflections, opt-in, desktop WebGPU only; never on WebGL2 or phones), ?gamut=p3|srgb (pin the canvas gamut) and ?tonemap=agx (the AgX tone curve, beside ACES and Khronos PBR Neutral).

Recipes#

Archviz client link (baked interior). The defaults already give SSR on bake-dominant scenes. For a link that renders identically on every client screen: &ssr=0.5&hdr=0&sheen=0.15.

Product on a white studio background (lit GLB). &env=studio,1.2&exposure=0.3&tbn=1 if the asset's normal map has a hard-seam unwrap; drop tbn otherwise.

Something looks wrong — is it the engine or the display? Add &hdr=0&scale=1&post=full. If it still looks wrong, it is content or a bug; screenshots are tone-mapped to SDR and prove nothing about HDR.

Frame time on a laptop GPU. &profile=1&scale=1, read the frame row, then &scale=0.6: if frame barely moves, the cost is in resolution-independent passes (cull, vg-cull) and DRS cannot help.

Battery-friendly kiosk. &render=demand — the engine parks between interactions; streaming and the heartbeat keep running.

In an embed#

The SDK exposes the user-facing subset as options rather than URL knobs: render ("demand" default), hdr (SDR default — your page's colours never shift uninvited), quality: "4k", and verbs for the look — setExposure(ev), setSun(), setMaterial(), setDepthOfField(), setEnvironment(url). See the Embed SDK reference.

What the knobs are measured against#

The lit path is gated against Blender EEVEE ground truth (web/test/fidelity-lit.mjs, 64×64 mean ΔE76 below 9 per view, achieved 1.7–7.0 on the scripted subjects), and the baked path against the source bake itself (web/test/fidelity.mjs, ΔE below 6). SSR has its own locality and energy gate (web/test/fix-verify-ssr.mjs) because the references were rendered without reflections. Goldens and both fidelity harnesses run in SDR, so ?hdr never changes a tested pixel.
